cues.text: We are living in the most sedentary era in modern history.
cues.en: We are living in the most sedentary era in modern history.

cues.text: is toxic.

cues.en: Let's start with the healthiest people among us to use as an example.

cues.text: In one study, when highly trained endurance athletes were forced to bed rest,
cues.en: In one study, when highly trained endurance athletes were forced to bed rest,
cues.zh: 在一項研究中， 受過嚴格訓練的耐力運動員 被要求臥床休息， 他們的心肺適能在短短三天內

cues.en: with no movement.

cues.en: This isn’t unique to highly trained endurance athletes.
cues.zh: 而這種情況並不只發生在 專業耐力運動員身上。 如果你找一位健康的普通成年人，

cues.en: Now, this isn't about missing a workout or two.

cues.en: The toxicity comes from when movement begins to disappear from your life.

cues.en: And this begs the question, why isn't exercise alone enough?
cues.zh: 這也讓我們思考： 為什麼光靠運動還不夠？

cues.en: Part of the answer lies in our muscles.
cues.zh: 部分答案藏在肌肉裡。

cues.en: Our muscles are more than just a machinery that power movement.

cues.en: Our muscles are like sponges for blood sugar.

cues.zh: 但如果長時間不使用肌肉， 它就會變成一塊乾癟的海綿， 幾乎什麼都吸不進去。

cues.text: like a dry and shriveled-up sponge, not really good at soaking up anything.
cues.en: like a dry and shriveled-up sponge, not really good at soaking up anything.
cues.zh: 它就會變成一塊乾癟的海綿， 幾乎什麼都吸不進去。

cues.en: if you get little to no movement the rest of your day.
cues.zh: 那塊海綿最後還是會再次乾掉。 所以我們該怎麼辦？

cues.en: So what do we do?
cues.zh: 所以我們該怎麼辦？

cues.en: Well, we need to keep the sponge moist.
cues.zh: 答案是：讓海綿持續保持濕潤。

cues.en: The tobacco industry.

cues.zh: 但當時正值工業時代，

cues.en: so that these workers could get their fix in small, short doses,

cues.text: a few minutes at a time throughout the day.

cues.text: And if sitting truly is the new smoking,
cues.en: And if sitting truly is the new smoking,
cues.zh: 如果真像俗話說的， 久坐就是這個時代的吸菸，

cues.text: The question that we asked in my lab is, what’s the least amount of “movement breaks” that we need
cues.en: The question that we asked in my lab is, what’s the least amount of “movement breaks” that we need
cues.zh: 因此，我的研究團隊提出一個問題： 究竟需要多少次「活動休息時間」， 才能抵消長期久坐帶來的傷害？

cues.en: in order to offset the harms of being highly sedentary?

cues.text: And the answer we found was a five-minute walk every half hour.

cues.text: This reduced the blood sugar spike after eating by about 60 percent.

cues.text: to manage their blood sugar levels.
cues.en: to manage their blood sugar levels.
cues.zh: 幾乎等同於服用控制血糖藥物 所能帶來的改善。

cues.en: The cool part is that our participants weren't sprinting or even walking fast.

cues.text: Now I want to be honest.

cues.zh: 我跟大家坦誠，

cues.text: are five-minute breaks every hour or every half hour.

cues.en: The truth is that when I found out that this was the answer,

cues.zh: 然而，曾幾何時，我們竟然相信， 連續八小時盯著螢幕一動也不動， 才是最有效率的工作方式。
